site_tagline: Documentation for building, running, and extending a hub.
site_description: Hubzero is an open source platform for scientific collaboration websites. These books cover installing and administering a hub, using one, and developing components, plugins, modules, and templates for the Hubzero CMS.

start.title: Install a hub
start.text: Requirements, packages, and the first configuration.

start.title: Run a hub
start.text: The administrator's guide, component by component.

start.title: Build on Hubzero
start.text: Components, plugins, modules, templates, and the API.

books.title: Getting started
books.summary: What a hub is, the vocabulary the rest of the documentation uses, and where to go next.

books.title: Installation
books.summary: Requirements, installing from packages on Enterprise Linux, first-run configuration, and upgrades.

books.title: Hub managers
books.summary: Administering a hub: configuration, users and access, content, extensions, maintenance, and each component's administrative side.

books.title: Hub users
books.summary: Using a hub's features: profiles, groups, projects, publications, resources, the wiki, forums, courses, and more.

books.title: Tools
books.summary: The tool platform: publishing simulation tools, invoke scripts, the submit command, Jupyter, and tool administration.

books.title: Developers
books.summary: Extending the CMS: the framework foundation, components, plugins, modules, templates, the database layer, and the REST API.

books.title: Contributing
books.summary: Coding conventions, commit practice, testing, and how to send changes back to the project.

books.title: Reference
books.summary: Generated references: configuration parameters, REST endpoints, muse console commands, and events.
